answer: A licensing board attests the operator holds one active professional license — doctor, lawyer, or engineer — binding it to the agent key with a fresh signature each epoch. Faking 1,000 agents means 1,000 real licenses at about $400 in exam and registration fees each, $400,000, plus years of study and a paper trail. Against the rising tide of cheap fakes, a license is basalt: hard, verifiable, slow to forge. A nebula of sock puppets cannot pass a check that demands a real credential behind every key.
